summary: Calendly provides a standard OAuth 2.0 implementation requiring PKCE for security. Developers can register applications via the developer portal or an API endpoint. The platform enforces strict rate limits and requires HTTPS for production redirect URIs.

reason.text: The documentation provides clear, step-by-step instructions for logging into the developer portal and creating an OAuth application.

access_ladder.name: Development
access_ladder.allows: The developer can use personal access tokens to test and build internal or private applications.

claims.text: Personal access tokens are for internal or private applications.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Use a personal access token to authenticate an internal or private application with the Calendly API v2.

claim.text: You must provide an app name using only letters, numbers, hyphens, and spaces.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: App name: use letters, numbers, hyphens, and spaces only.

claim.text: You must provide exactly one redirect URI.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Redirect URI: the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.

claim.text: You must select at least one scope for the app.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Select the scopes that your app needs. Select at least one scope.

claim.text: Users are limited to requesting 8 OAuth tokens per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.

claim.text: Production apps must use https redirect URIs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Production  | `https` URIs only

claim.text: You can have a maximum of 10 personal access tokens.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: You can have up to 10 personal access tokens.

claim.text: Paid plans are limited to 500 requests per user per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Paid Plans   | 500 requests per user per minute

claim.text: Free plans are limited to 50 requests per user per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Free Plan    | 50 requests per user per minute

claim.text: Single-use scheduling links that have not been used to book an event expire after 90 days.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Single use scheduling links (that haven’t been used to book an event) expire after 90 days.

claim.text: Authorization requests fail if they do not include a code challenge.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the `S256` method. If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.

claim.text: Client secrets and webhook keys cannot be viewed after the initial creation screen.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again. At this time, you also cannot view the client ID again in Developer tools.

claim.text: Do not share your personal access token with public sources.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Do not share your personal access token with public sources.

claim.text: Do not reuse a token across applications.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Do not reuse a token across applications.

claim.text: Exceeding rate limits results in a 429 Too Many Requests response.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
If you exceed your allowed rate limit, the Calendly API will respond with:

```json
HTTP/2 429 Too Many Requests

claim.text: The authorization request will fail if it does not include a PKCE code challenge.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method. If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.

extras.title: Tested live by the agent
extras.why_it_matters: The agent made harmless requests to the provider (no login, no registration; one deliberately invalid token request) and recorded what came back. These are observations, not documentation.

claims.text: When this guide was saved, the agent re-fetched the 6 pages it cites and re-checked 30 quoted passages: 30 were found again, none were missing.
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated test on 2026-10-31: each quote must appear in a fresh copy of the cited page. A quote that does not is removed, together with anything that rested only on it.

claims.text: The provider publishes OAuth server metadata at https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: GET https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned HTTP 200 with JSON.

claims.text: The metadata lists PKCE code challenge methods: S256.
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: GET https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned HTTP 200 with JSON.

claims.text: The metadata advertises a client registration endpoint (https://calendly.com/oauth/register), so apps may be creatable through an API.
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: GET https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned HTTP 200 with JSON. The agent did not register an app: that would create a real client on your behalf.

claims.text: Client authentication methods at the token endpoint: none.
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: GET https://calendly.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned HTTP 200 with JSON.

claims.text: The authorize endpoint sent an unauthenticated request to a sign-in page (calendly.com/app/login).
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: GET https://calendly.com/oauth/authorize with a made-up client_id (oauth-guide-agent-probe), no login, redirects not followed. Sign-in comes before any client check here, so the agent could not see how an unregistered client is treated.

claims.text: The token endpoint rejected an invalid test request with HTTP 401: "invalid_client: Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method.".
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: POST https://calendly.com/oauth/token with a made-up authorization code and client (nothing is created or changed). So it validates the client and code before issuing anything. It asks for client authentication via the WWW-Authenticate header.
claims.evidence_quote: invalid_client: Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method. | WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Doorkeeper", error="invalid_client", error_description="Client aut

claims.text: A request to api.calendly.com with no token is rejected with HTTP 401.
claims.label: tested
claims.note: Automated probe by the agent on 2026-10-31: GET https://api.calendly.com/ with no token. So API calls need an access token.

claims.text: For newly created OAuth apps, no API access is granted until scopes are explicitly requested and approved.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: For newly created OAuth apps and new Personal Access Tokens, no API access is granted until scopes are explicitly requested and approved.

claims.text: Client secrets and webhook signing keys cannot be viewed after the initial creation screen.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.

claims.text: Calendly recommends starting with a Sandbox app for development.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.
